Museum of Modern Art

Modern Sol

Core tokens, baseline type, and the Tailwind adapter on one page.

This app is the first living review surface for the fork. It proves that the generated core.css primitives and the CSS-first Tailwind adapter can render against the same token source as first-class packages without a legacy shim in the middle.

Build Surface

Static docs build

Generated under apps/docs/dist, verified in CI with npm run check:docs.

Adapter Shape

Tailwind v4, CSS-first

@theme inline, @utility, and @custom-variant project Sol values into Tailwind without duplicating the source of truth.

Typography Fixtures

Core CSS

Baseline-trimmed heading

The .sol-typography contract trims the bounding box with pseudo-elements and keeps the MoMA Sans metrics explicit instead of burying them in a Sass atom graph.

Classes used: sol-typography, sol-weight-bold, sol-baseline-solid, sol-size-large

Tailwind Adapter

Tailwind-native Sol typography

Sol tokens now project into Tailwind text, font, tracking, color, and breakpoint utilities without a JS preset.

Classes used: text-sol-large, font-sol-condensed, tracking-sol-bold, leading-sol-body, sol-desktop:text-sol-large-desktop

Core + Tailwind

Variable utilities on the core primitive

The Tailwind package sets the same variables that core.css consumes, so the integration surface is explicit and inspectable.

Responsive Alias

The desktop size alias is generated from the same token JSON.

Resize past the desktop breakpoint to verify sol-desktop:text-sol-large-desktop.

Runtime States

Session Color

Brand 1

The accent now follows the same semantic session variable the runtime writes.

This fixture cycles through the runtime sequence and updates --color--session and --color--session--rgb on document.documentElement.

Tailwind variant

The custom variant targets the explicit [data-high-contrast] state only.
